text:
IncidentBot: PAGER: Cache integrity anomaly detected. Error-rate for prefix lookups (kv/prefix) > 7% across us-west-2 serving pool for model redwood-3b. Automatic prefetch backoff triggered. Root ts: 2024-06-15T10:21:10Z

erin_oncall: oncall here — I'm seeing streaming errors and client 5xx spikes for a few tenants. correlation with hot-prefix lookups + KV misses. gonna start live mitigations: disable prefetch for affected prefixes and enable correctness cache-bypass for the path. Paging @maya for tenant rate/quotas.

samir: which tenants are noisy? quick grep shows high qps from acme-inc and weatherai-prod hitting the same prefix keys. also a smaller spike from test-tenant-3.

jess: I'm going to apply per-tenant traffic shaping: set acme-inc burst=100, steady=10r/s; weatherai-prod burst=80 steady=8r/s. will also throttle streaming chunking to reduce backend load.

maya: applying rate caps now. also flipping safe-mode routing to fallback model-variant small-latency for the affected routes to reduce KV pressure. will push changes in 2m.

erin_oncall: action log: disabling prefetch for prefixes with >1000 QPS and enabling kv-prefix bypass for correctness for those requests. this is expected to increase token cost but should stop incorrect responses. monitor for client-facing regressions.

samir: command I ran to patch the cache config (for audit):

```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap cache-config -p '{"data":{"prefetch_threshold":"1000","prefetch_enabled":"false"}}'
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/cache-controller -- /bin/sh -c "service reload cache-config"
```

jess: confirming: applied tenant quota edits and per-route rate limits. also disabled async prefetch worker on the hotpool.

support_engineer: raising CS ticket: CS-4982 — customers impacted: acme-inc (degraded streaming), weatherai-prod (delayed tokens). Notifying account leads. Any ETA on rollback?

erin_oncall: rollback plan: re-enable prefetch + revert bypass only after KV error-rate < 1% for 10 continuous minutes and overall 5xxs back to baseline. will post metric thresholds to the incident.

maya: live telemetry: kv-error-rate for affected prefixes down from 7.2% -> 1.8% 6 minutes after changes. QPS on backend reduced ~45%. continuing to monitor.

samir: saving a degraded-state snapshot for postmortem: s3://redwood-ops/incident-snapshots/3512345670-cache-integrity-surge-20240615.tar.gz

erin_oncall: handing off to oncall_manager in 20m for overnight carry. leaving runbook notes: 1) keep prefetch off for prefixes >1k qps; 2) keep kv-bypass enabled for correctness until stable; 3) customer comms owned by CS (ticket CS-4982).

oncall_manager: taking over. thanks @erin_oncall and team. I'll keep the mitigation in place and coordinate with eng-runtime for a targeted fix. will schedule a quick postmortem and include regression test for prefetch eviction. tagging postmortem label: cache-integrity-surge.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT update: status=mitigating, impact=degraded streaming responses for 3 tenants, mitigations=tenant-rate-limits + prefetch disabled + kv-bypass enabled. next update in 15m or on significant change.
